- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% of recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior 5-day avg), model often overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; add 1–2% upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.
- For 30-day forecasts, model exhibits strong lag: true price often diverges from forecast by +2–4% in first 5–7 days; apply early correction by +1–2% to first 5 days of forecast.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model tends to average out; use sentiment-weighted median of recent 3–5 days to anchor forecast.
- If true outcome shows sudden drop after forecast peak, model often fails to anticipate policy or supply shocks; add 1–3% downward buffer if sentiment turns negative within 3 days.
